intelligence.essence: "Merged" is a claim about a pointer, not a fact about content: a stale merge ref can fabricate a RED on a ghost tree (SN-0443), a squash merge erases the head SHA so only a four-step proof makes MERGED into MERGED-VERIFIED-AT-TIP (SN-0447), three fallback merges with tree=head-tree silently dropped 34 files while GitHub showed all three merged (SN-0539), and a SHA that is merely an ancestor of the live tip is stale, not false (SN-0534). The tip is the truth — everything else is re-anchored to it or it is not evidence.
intelligence.human_view: In a system where many lanes merge all day, the most dangerous sentence is "it's merged." This block learned that merged can mean three different things — merged into a ghost tree, merged with files silently dropped, merged with a red that changed its nature at the boundary — and that each has a mechanical proof that settles it. The essence is the habit of never trusting the pointer: prove ancestry, prove the bytes, replay the chain, and re-anchor every claim to the tip that exists now.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine mailing a letter in a new envelope. "The letter was mailed" doesn't prove the letter inside is still your letter. So you check: the envelope is really on the truck, the words inside match yours exactly, letter for letter. And if three friends each add a page to a story one after another, you can't check the final story by comparing each page to the first draft — each page was added to the story as it grew. You rebuild it in the same order, or your check invents mistakes that aren't there.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's the old rule about deeds and titles: the stamp on the paperwork is only as good as the contents underneath. A deed can be stamped "transferred" while pages are missing from the file. The careful clerk checks the actual pages against the original, in order, and counts what's there — not what the stamp claims. And when two clerks recorded the river's height at different hours, neither lied; the river moved. Check the time and the place before calling anyone wrong.
intelligence.ai_view: On every merge and every tip claim: refresh the branch before reading its red, and run the three-way discriminator (SN-0443); prove merged content with ancestry + blob identity + honest CI + ledger recompute, naming the residual gap (SN-0447); re-anchor claimed SHAs by compare before judging them (SN-0534); test the containment precondition before any tree=head-tree fallback merge, and verify the result against a real local merge (SN-0539); verify chains by replaying merge-tree in order, never by fixed-base simulation (SN-0542); and after any merge — especially a red one — reclassify every open RED on the new tip before repairing anything (SN-0578).
intelligence.what_it_means: Six notes make one discipline: the tip is the only truth, and every merge artifact — ref, pointer, stamp, classification, claimed SHA — is a claim about it that decays or deceives in a named way. A cold reader holding only this essence can prove what is actually on main after any merge, which is the ground every other verdict stands on.
whats_inside: Re-sync the branch to main before reading a CI red; the three-way discriminator (head / merge-delta / stale ref) runs before any code diagnosis (SN-0443).
MERGED becomes MERGED-VERIFIED-AT-TIP only via the four-step proof: ancestry, zero blob drift, honest CI read, ledger recompute (SN-0447).
A claimed tip SHA is re-anchored by ancestry before it is judged: ancestor = stale, diverged = violation (SN-0534).
tree=head-tree requires the containment precondition, tested before every fallback merge; "clean" never means "contains the base" (SN-0539).
Sequential merges are verified by replaying git's real machinery in order — merge-bases shift (SN-0542).
At the merge boundary, every RED is reclassified on the new tip; a red merge converts a PR problem into a base defect (SN-0578).
